newsitem.title: USA: Bradies close mixed, awaiting Fed's decision.
newsitem.headline: Bradies close mixed, awaiting Fed's decision.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices traded narrowly mixed on Monday ahead of the Federal Reserve's key policy meeting Tuesday, Brady bond traders said.

Dealers reported minimal trading activity with opinions split over whether the Fed will raise U.S. rates. In a Reuters survey, a slight majority of U.S. primary dealers believed the Fed would keep key rates unchanged.
The Fed generally announces its decision around 1415 EDT/1815 GMT.
"Nobody wants to do anything until tomorrow," one Brady bond trader said.
Of the most liquid Brady instruments, the Argentine FRBs slipped 1/8 to 92-1/4, while Brazil "C" bonds were unchanged at 76 bid.
Venezuelan DCBs dipped 1/4 to 89-5/8, and FLIRBs lost 1/2 to 90-1/8, while Mexican discounts gained 1/4 to 91-1/4 bid.
"This has probably been my lowest volume day in a year-and-a-half," one Brady bond trader said. "Everybody set up their books ahead of time."
Joe Petry, chief economist Latin America at Citicorp Securities, said the market seemed to be fairly balanced in its Brady positions.
"We're a little bit cautious going in," Petry said. "I would say theres more downside than upside right now. The market probably hasn't fully hasn't discounted a move tomorrow."
